title: FlattenOptions.inheritDoc(false) changes nothing: leaves still inherit their ancestor's documentation
rationale: The repository's signature pathology, in the newest code on the branch. inheritDoc is declared, defaulted, validated, stored, exposed by a getter and documented as 'Whether a leaf with no doc inherits the nearest ancestor record's. Default true' - and a grep across src/main finds ZERO reads of options.inheritDoc(). walkRecord computes recordDoc and fieldDoc unconditionally. The only unit test named for it passed inheritDoc(true) and asserted the doc was present, so it could only ever pass; it has been rewritten to assert the current wrong behaviour and to name this row. Nothing in the repository could previously observe this. The recorded renderings here are byte-identical to the inheritance fixture's despite the opposite configuration, and that identity IS the finding.
catchesBugClass: Dead configuration: a builder method that validates, stores, is exposed by a getter, and is never read. The corpus already has one of these in reconstructor-maxdepth-is-a-dead-control and this is the second. Wiring the control up flips both the verdict and the probe and turns the build red on purpose.
cannotCatch: A round-trip assertion alone cannot see this - the flatten succeeds and every column is present, which is why a losslessness-only harness reports nothing. It also cannot tell whether the right repair is to honour the flag or to delete it; both make this row stale, and that choice is a human one.

predicted.detail: The consumer asked for declared-only documentation and got inherited documentation, with no error and no diagnostic. The probe's two arms render identically, which is the inert-control proof, and it is only meaningful because the sibling probes on collisionPolicy and inheritRecordProperties expect DIFFERENT and get it.

probe.note: These two must render identically only for as long as the control is dead; the day inheritDoc is honoured this flips.
